statement: Find all solutions in positive integers to $(n+1)^k - 1 = n!$
Each day $289$ students are divided into $17$ groups of $17$. No two students are ever in the same group more than once. What is the largest number of days for which this can be done?

Given a regular dodecahedron of side $a$, take two pairs of opposite faces $E, E'$ and $F, F'$. For the pair $E, E'$, take the line joining the centers of the faces and place points $A$ and $C$ on this line each at distance $m$ outside one of the faces. Similarly place $B$ and $D$ on the line joining the centers of $F, F'$. Show that $ABCD$ is a rectangle and find the ratio of its side lengths.

Triangle $ABC$ has $\angle A = 90^\circ$. For a point $D$ on side $BC$, let $E$ and $F$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $D$ to $AB$ and $AC$ respectively. For which point $D$ is $EF$ minimized?

$ABCD$ is any convex quadrilateral. Squares with centers $E$, $F$, $G$, $H$ are constructed on the outside of edges $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, and $DA$ respectively. Show that $EG$ and $FH$ are equal and perpendicular.

A solitaire board has a piece on every square except the central square. A move consists of choosing three adjacent squares in a horizontal or vertical line with exactly two occupied and one empty: the two pieces are removed and one piece is placed on the empty square (one piece hops over the other). Is it possible to end with a single piece on the square marked $X$?
